metadata.evidence_scope: site-level Regulative Principle of Worship formulation
metadata.modeling_rule: The accessible page exposes no named author, so claims are modeled as site-level published content rather than assigned to an individual or automatically applied to every Jude 3-linked worship resource.

positions.summary: The Jude 3 page states that the Second Commandment regulates the entirety of how God is worshiped and identifies this principle as the Regulative Principle of Worship.
The page formulates the Regulative Principle positively as practicing what God has appointed in Scripture for worship and negatively as refusing modes of worship God has not appointed.
The page presents Westminster Confession of Faith 21.1 and Westminster Shorter Catechism 50–51 as confessional formulations of the Regulative Principle of Worship.
positions.boundary: This record captures Jude 3's appeal to the Standards and does not infer a position on every disputed application of the RPW.
